properties.label: Project source excerpt
properties.text:
# One document. More ways to use it.

## 01 — Less file management
A brief in .docx. A deck in .pptx. A script in .txt. Images in .png. Audio in .wav. Video in .mp4. Then the project files, exports, and “final-final” versions.

The hard part is not the extensions. It is keeping the same idea intact across them.

## 02 — One source, many outputs
A Forma document holds the shared creative context: what we are making, who it is for, what it should say, and what must stay true.

Start there, then produce the form the audience needs. Formats still exist at delivery; they stop being separate places to manage the meaning. Revise the source, then review and regenerate the affected outputs.

## 03 — Changes become useful context
Event-log-based management records the work as changes, not only as a latest saved state. A shared record helps people coordinate: what changed and what needs attention.

The same foundation that supports multiplayer collaboration can support agents working at different levels—from a local suggestion to a specialist production task—with changes that can be reviewed.

## 04 — Assistance that can improve
A useful loop is simple: suggest → review → decide → remember → improve the next pass.

Accepted decisions can inform later suggestions, within the right permissions and scope. Memory should preserve useful context, not turn every draft into an irreversible preference. This is a path to better assistance, not automatic model retraining.

## 05 — Room for the next experience
The document need not belong to one interface. A standalone lead-gen experience could use it to create a tailored result. A newly capable model could use the same goals and constraints for live video direction.

These are expansion paths, not promises that those experiences are live today. The benefit is a reusable source that new tools can work from.

## 06 — Let Forma show it
Compare the slideshow, two-speaker podcast, and crew-directed video made from this document. Different forms, same central claims. That is the test of the workflow.
